session.goal: Investigate and fix the genuine Echo recording restart failure documented in docs/observed-recording-gate-failure.md, preserving session and lock safety with a regression test, focused and workspace validation, and independent review.

plan.summary: Repair the recording gate acquisition race that can reject a new session after the preceding session has dropped its lock, and prove the restart behavior without weakening lock or session safety.
plan.overview: Reproduce the documented unit failure in the isolated workspace, trace ToggleSession gate and lock ownership transitions, then make the smallest lease-layer correction and add a deterministic regression test for the stale-gate/no-live-lock condition. Preserve exclusive gate serialization, verified live-owner detection, token-scoped intents, and cleanup ownership. Validate the focused behavior and canonical workspace suite before independent review.
requirements: Reproduce the documented recording restart failure before editing.
Identify why recording.gate can remain locked after the prior session drops.
Allow a new recording session only when no verified live recording-lock owner exists.
Preserve session identity, token-scoped intent behavior, and lock safety for a live owner.
Add a regression test for the failure condition.
Run focused validation and the workspace test gate.
Do not push, merge, or release.
decisions: The repair scope is limited to crates/echo recording lease acquisition and its unit tests; no product API or protocol change is authorized.
The canonical whole-repository gate is `RUSTUP_HOME=/home/vriesd/.rustup cargo test --workspace`, as recorded by the observed failure report.
Focused behavior will use the existing test filter against `rec::tests::toggle_starts_stops_and_can_restart`; this isolates the documented restart contract.
The implementation must not remove or bypass the gate lock; it must preserve serialization while resolving stale lock-state observation safely.

features.title: Repair recording gate restart
features.summary: Reproduce the reported restart rejection, correct gate/lock acquisition handling, and add a regression test proving a dropped prior session can restart without admitting concurrent live owners.
validation: Regression test exercises a prior-session gate release with no live recording.lock owner and verifies restart; existing live-owner serialization tests remain valid.

evidence.requirement: The complete Rust workspace remains passing after the recording lease repair.
evidence.environment: Isolated Linux workspace with the documented Rust toolchain home.

packet.summary: Current workspace-versus-HEAD feature diff: modified crates/echo/src/rec/lease.rs and crates/echo/src/rec/tests.rs only (43 insertions, 8 deletions); no additions, deletions, renames, type changes, executable-mode changes, generated artifacts, documentation changes, or unrelated pre-existing work reported by git status. lease.rs retries a contended recording.gate for up to 32 ms when recording.lock has no live owner, but preserves Busy for a live owner; tests.rs adds a regression that holds the prior gate without recording.lock, releases it, and asserts restart. Current-source evidence: focused regression and restart tests previously passed; canonical RUSTUP_HOME=/home/vriesd/.rustup cargo test --workspace passed with full captured output at Flow revision 11 (receipt d5d5e2ee-191d-496d-b1cc-c2192987dfff). Inspect concurrency/locking behavior, retry bounds, error behavior, and regression determinism.

findings.summary: The new regression does not deterministically exercise the contended-gate retry path.
findings.evidence: crates/echo/src/rec/tests.rs:1091-1099 signals before the worker calls try_start_in, then relies on a 5 ms sleep before unlocking. The worker may remain unscheduled until after unlock, allowing the test to pass without ever observing WouldBlock or executing the retry added at crates/echo/src/rec/lease.rs:170-183. This does not prove the required stale-gate/no-live-lock regression behavior.
